transcript_location_inventory.excluded_directories_rationale: All directories starting with -private-tmp- are ephemeral test/eval directories created for evaluation runs and reused across sessions. They are not real development repositories.

pi_transcripts.structure: Directory of per-session .jsonl files at ~/.pi/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl, analogous to Claude Code project structure but without per-repo grouping
pi_transcripts.note: Pi transcripts exist and are structured differently from Claude Code: there is no per-repo grouping (no ~source directory mapping like ~/.claude/projects); all sessions are flat-listed in ~/.pi/agent/sessions/. For this audit, Pi sessions should be included if analysis scope covers multiple harnesses.
pi_transcripts.extractor_support: added in task 2.3 — dev/eval/audit/extract.py now auto-detects Pi format (by checking first line for {type: session, version: 3}), parses JSONL message structure with bash/subagent tool calls, and extracts recall calls, dispatch events with multiple tasks per subagent call, and engram commands. See extract_transcript_pi() for implementation and extract.py for format-detection logic.

sampling_plan.description: Representative sample design for memory-loop-audit, ensuring coverage across all repos and transcript types

dispatch_type_sample.classification_method: Read first 50 lines of each sampled subagent transcript; check for fork boilerplate ("inherit", "inherited", "conversation context", "parent", "prior turn"); check file path for workflow indicator (/subagents/workflows/); classify accordingly
dispatch_type_sample.note: SAMPLE-BASED ESTIMATE. Fresh-context subagents may exist but were not found in the 26-file sample across all repos; a full scan of all subagent files may reveal some.

proposed_sample.reasoning: Must span EVERY repo (to avoid single-repo bias per vault note 110) with both main and subagent/workflow transcripts. Precedent used 40 transcripts (25 subagent + 15 main) across 5 repos; scaled to 8 repos: ~64 transcripts (40 subagent + 24 main), sampled to ensure each repo appears. Main repos with heavy transcripts (engram, phone-llm, targ) sampled proportionally more heavily.
proposed_sample.dispatch_type_sample_estimate: SAMPLE-BASED ESTIMATE from 26 sampled subagent transcripts across all repos: fork 73.1% (19/26), workflow 26.9% (7/26), fresh-context 0% (0/26). Note: Fresh-context subagents may exist but were not found in this sample; may need targeted search if important for analysis.

sampling_plan.window_sizing_strategy: Each window maximum 150KB, split at natural turn boundaries (JSON turn objects). For files under 500KB, no windowing needed. For files over 500KB, split into multiple windows with boundaries written to this file.

point_in_time_check_preconditions.vault_git_history_interpretation: The vault has 42 commits with densest activity in 2026-08 (30 commits on a single day 2026-08-29). For moments dated 2026-06-02 through 2026-08-29, an EXACT (DERIVED) point-in-time check is possible. For moments predating 2026-06-02, fall back to APPROXIMATE (ESTIMATE) check using chunk ingestion date filtering.

chunk_ingestion_timestamp.code_snippet: IngestedAt time.Time `json:"ingested_at,omitzero"` //nolint:tagliatelle // index schema uses snake_case like .vec.json
chunk_ingestion_timestamp.comment: IngestedAt is the wall-clock time this chunk was first written to the index. Zero for legacy records (pre-D5); backfilled on first merge. Tag is omitzero, not omitempty: omitempty has no effect on a struct like time.Time, so a zero value would serialize; omitzero (Go 1.24+) omits it, letting legacy records decode IngestedAt=zero (the migration sentinel).
chunk_ingestion_timestamp.test_file: internal/chunk/ingestedat_test.go (validates round-trip serialization and legacy record handling)
